title: High-NA’s Obituary Was Premature
gist: Daniel Nenni argues High-NA EUV's obituary was premature: Intel is shipping Panther Lake with select High-NA layers at yields matching NXE, Intel/ASML report 1M+ wafers processed (not all production), Samsung targets DRAM volume by 2028, and TSMC plans advanced-node volume from 2030. He expects staggered, layer-by-layer adoption driven by full patterning economics, with the halved exposure field a structural limit addressed by 12-inch masks (pilot 2031, production readiness 2033).

insights.claim: ASML announced in July that selected layers of a subset of Intel Panther Lake processors are manufactured with High-NA EUV, dual-qualified against conventional EUV with yields matching the NXE platform.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: High-NA has entered a shipping product flow, de-risking ASML's next-generation tool ramp.
insights.quote: Those layers were dual-qualified against conventional EUV, with yields matching the existing NXE platform.
insights.locator: The strongest evidence comes from Intel

insights.claim: High-NA use in Panther Lake does not mean every Panther Lake processor uses High-NA or that Intel 18A depends on it.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Caveat limits how much High-NA volume to infer from Intel's adoption.
insights.quote: It does not mean every Panther Lake processor uses High-NA, or that Intel 18A depends on it.
insights.locator: The strongest evidence comes from Intel

insights.claim: By September, Intel and ASML reported more than one million wafers processed on High-NA across certification, R&D and production, with overlay, throughput and availability meeting Intel's expectations; this is not one million customer production wafers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Accumulated operating experience reduces tool-maturity risk.
insights.quote: the figure is not one million customer production wafers

insights.claim: Daniel Nenni argues the skeptics confused a delayed High-NA adoption curve with a technology running out of road, and recent announcements make the obituary harder to defend.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Counters bearish narratives on ASML's High-NA EXE franchise.
insights.quote: It became tempting to confuse a delayed adoption curve with a technology running out of road.

insights.claim: TSMC intends to introduce High-NA EUV into advanced-node volume manufacturing starting in 2030, with C.C. Wei emphasising maturity and reasonable cost as adoption conditions on the October earnings call.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Firm TSMC timeline anchors ASML High-NA demand around end of decade.

insights.claim: Samsung plans to introduce High-NA EUV into DRAM volume manufacturing by 2028.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: DRAM may be an earlier High-NA volume adopter than leading-edge logic at TSMC.
insights.quote: Samsung, meanwhile, plans to introduce High-NA into DRAM volume manufacturing by 2028.

insights.claim: High-NA adoption will be staggered across customers and applications rather than a universal switchover, with existing EUV continuing to improve and compete for layers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: High-NA unit ramp likely gradual; low-NA EUV demand remains durable.
insights.quote: High-NA must win each allocation through measurable manufacturing advantages.

insights.claim: Being first to install a lithography tool and being first to extract an attractive return from it are different achievements, as TSMC's cost-driven insertion point shows.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Early adoption by Intel is not by itself a competitive advantage over TSMC.
insights.quote: Being first to install a tool and being first to extract an attractive return are different achievements.

insights.claim: Raising numerical aperture from 0.33 to 0.55 improves resolution, and where it replaces multiple exposures the savings can extend beyond scanner throughput by cutting process steps and variation.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Correct economic comparison is full patterning-sequence cost and yield, not tool price.
insights.quote: The relevant comparison is therefore the cost and yield of the complete patterning sequence, rather than the purchase price of one machine.

insights.claim: High-NA's anamorphic optics halve the exposure field with today's mask format, creating layout constraints or stitching requirements for large designs, which Intel says it handles through floorplanning and stitching.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Halved field is a structural headwind for large AI die on High-NA.

insights.claim: ASML and TSMC are pursuing 12-inch photomasks with a pilot line targeted for 2031 and advanced-node production readiness for 2033.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Long timeline shows the ecosystem work still required for full High-NA field size.

insights.claim: Whether High-NA reaches broad adoption will depend on which layers benefit, scanner reliability, upstream/downstream changes and whether savings survive full production accounting.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Investors should watch layer-count and uptime disclosures more than announcements.
